open_obligations: Check whether the union ceiling is attainable by any single model or only an oracle combination.
Note that models are 1-9B, not GPT-4 family.
Check how much PGR values would change under the alternative ceiling.
out.other_title: Performance gap recovered (PGR) metric for weak-to-strong generalization
out.rationale: Burns et al. define PGR relative to a strong ceiling model finetuned on ground truth labels. Goel et al. report that counting complementary knowledge (union of correct predictions of the strong elicited model and weak supervisor) gives a ceiling of +14.1 versus +11.2 from ground-truth elicitation, implying the standard ceiling underestimates what is achievable; averages are over 15 tasks and 12 small-model pairs.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether the strong ceiling used in PGR (strong model finetuned on ground truth) is the right upper bound for weak-to-strong gains

text: Table 3 reports, relative to an initial strong-student accuracy of 75.1%, gaps of +4.1 for the weak supervisor and +7.4 for the weak-to-strong trained student, a previous ceiling estimate from ground-truth elicitation of +11.2, and a ceiling of +14.1 from the union of correct predictions of the strong elicited model and the weak supervisor.
title: Higher weak-to-strong ceiling when complementary knowledge is counted (+14.1 vs +11.2)
